summary: Regime‑aware Wikipedia ingestion module — structuring the world's largest public knowledge base through an RTT lens. Extends the NIST 4‑file domain pattern with 7 Wikipedia‑specific cross‑domain files covering temporal regime analysis, consensus mechanics, knowledge graph integration, and cross‑language regime comparison. 15 knowledge domains × 4 standard files + 11 infrastructure files.

wikidata_sparql.purpose: Structured entity data — 120M+ items as Q/P triplets

database_dumps.purpose: Full corpus snapshots for bulk analysis

quarry_sql.purpose: Direct SQL queries against wiki replicas

structural_mappings._note: How Wikipedia's native structures map to RTT concepts
structural_mappings.article_structure: regime_declaration — each article declares what a concept IS
structural_mappings.wikidata_qid_pid: dimensional_addressing — Q‑numbers and P‑numbers as universal concept coordinates
structural_mappings.revision_history: temporal_regime_data — how knowledge evolves; edit frequency = regime stability signal
structural_mappings.talk_pages: coherence_drift_surface — where consensus is negotiated and structural disagreements surface
structural_mappings.category_taxonomy: regime_hierarchy — Wikipedia's category tree as a native regime classification
structural_mappings.portals: domain_front_doors — equivalent to TF index.html module entry points
structural_mappings.edit_wars: regime_transitions — conflict between competing structural claims reveals regime boundaries
structural_mappings.featured_article_process: validation_corridor — quality assurance as structural integrity verification
structural_mappings.deletion_debates: regime_collapse_detection — when the community decides a concept lacks structural standing
structural_mappings.npov_policy: coherence_operator — Neutral Point of View as RTT's structural invariant
structural_mappings.cross_language_articles: cultural_regime_comparison — same concept in 300+ languages reveals regime variance

similarities: Same 4-file domain pattern (overview, regime_alignment, student_exercises, triadic_awareness)
differences: Wikipedia has temporal depth (revision history) — NIST is static/authoritative
Wikipedia has consensus mechanics (talk pages, NPOV) — NIST has institutional authority
Wikipedia has Wikidata (120M+ structured entities, CC0) — NIST has no equivalent graph
Wikipedia has cross-language regime variance (300+ languages) — NIST is English-only
Wikipedia has edit wars as regime transition signals — NIST has no equivalent
Wikipedia requires 7 additional cross-domain files for these unique surfaces

what_tf_adds: Regime declaration — every Wikipedia article implicitly declares a regime; TF makes this explicit
Temporal regime analysis — edit history becomes a structural evolution timeline
Consensus as coherence — NPOV policy reframed as a structural invariant, not just editorial policy
Dimensional addressing — Wikidata Q/P-numbers as universal concept coordinates
Cross-language regime comparison — same concept across cultures reveals structural variance
Student exercises — active learning through regime-aware Wikipedia engagement
